policies.title: Suriname: ordinary passports outside the named 21-country exception visa-free for tourism or family visits
policies.summary: The Government established unilateral visa abolition for all foreign nationalities for tourist or family visits, while current Ministry guidance names an exhaustive 21-country exception from 1 May 2023. The remaining catalog foreign ordinary-passport rows are therefore visa-free under that stated general rule and closed exception.
conditions: This policy applies only to foreign ordinary passports outside the current named 21-country exception and only to tourism or family visits, for a maximum stay of 90 days.

The 2022 general rule expressly covered all foreign nationalities; the current Ministry page identifies the precise nationalities for which it ceased to apply from 1 May 2023. No rule is inferred merely from omission.

The Entry Fee is a separate fee/voucher mechanism, not an ETA, eVisa, visa on arrival or visa-free exception. The Ministry says its PDF voucher is electronically sent after online payment; that issuance concerns the fee only.

Business, internship, work, residence, PSA, transit, diplomatic, service, special, official, international-organization and third-country-document routes are outside this ordinary tourist/family baseline. Final admission and other travel-document requirements are not established here.

policies.title: Suriname: 21 named ordinary-passport nationalities subject to visa requirement
policies.summary: Current Government guidance identifies these 21 nationalities as excluded from unilateral visa abolition from 1 May 2023, and BIBIS confirms their visa requirement was reinstated. This is a visa-required baseline, not a visa-on-arrival policy or a finding of electronically issued visas.
conditions: The Government directly names this closed 21-nationality cohort as excluded from unilateral visa abolition from 1 May 2023; BIBIS confirms the visa requirement was reinstated for the 21 countries.

The Government’s E-Visa directory and BIBIS explanation establish an authorized online application service, but the opened official workflow does not state that a final ordinary visitor visa for this whole cohort is issued electronically. It is consequently normalized as visa_required, not evisa.
No visa-on-arrival route is stated. The separate Government Entry Fee voucher is not treated as a visa, ETA, eVisa or visa-on-arrival status, and does not displace the visa requirement.

For Cuba, Dominican Republic and Venezuela, BIBIS says a tourist card was reintroduced alongside the visa for tourist, business and short-stay travel. This alternate document is retained as a condition, not a separate normalized status.

No visa duration, entries, extension, port, admission result, health, funds or onward-travel condition is inferred. Residence, PSA, transit, CARICOM, diplomatic, service, special, official, international-organization, business, work and third-country-document exceptions are outside this ordinary visitor baseline.

policies.title: Suriname nationals entering Suriname
policies.summary: The Surinamese civil-registration authority identifies the national passport and expressly ties emergency-passport eligibility to Surinamese nationality. This records the catalog home-nationality relationship, not a foreign visitor permission.
conditions: This is the citizenship/home relationship for a Surinamese national ordinary passport, not a finding about visa-free visitor admission or a substitute for travel-document, exit, criminal, health or final-entry rules.

conflicts.explanation: Haiti is not among the Government’s exact 21-country exception. The original all-foreign-nationalities abolition, read with the current closed exception, makes the ordinary tourist/family baseline visa-free.
